summary:
We developed the Smart Astronaut Health Monitor, an advanced telemetry and Edge-AI platform designed to safeguard crew members during spaceflight. The application integrates real-time wearable biometrics (ECG/PPG, SpO2, heart rate), volumetric 3D body composition mapping (InBody bio-impedance for fluid, muscle, and fat tracking), and microgravity fluid-shift simulations.

It addresses the critical challenge of deep-space health management by providing automated emergency protocols (such as hypoxia and tachycardia response checklists), predictive metabolic trajectories, and robust offline resilience that buffers encrypted Blackbox packets during orbital communication blackouts (LOS).

This project is vital because long-duration space missions involve severe physiological stressors—such as fluid redistribution (cephalad shift/SANS risk) and muscle atrophy—alongside communication delays where medical evacuation is impossible. By empowering astronauts and flight surgeons with autonomous Edge-AI diagnostics and continuous health tracking, our platform ensures crew safety, operational autonomy, and mission success on journeys to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
details:
Project Overview & Functionality

The Smart Astronaut Health Monitor is an advanced, real-time biometric telemetry and Edge-AI platform engineered to safeguard crew members during spaceflight missions. The application continuously streams and analyzes critical physiological vitals—including ECG/PPG waveforms, blood oxygen saturation ($\text{SpO}_2$), heart rate, and core body temperature. It features an interactive volumetric 3D body composition engine that maps InBody bio-impedance metrics (Total Body Water, skeletal muscle mass, and body fat) and simulates microgravity fluid shifts (cephalad pooling and SANS risk factors). Furthermore, it includes automated emergency response checklists (for hypoxia or tachycardia), a predictive AI metabolic trajectory timeline, and robust offline resilience that buffers encrypted Blackbox packets during orbital communication blackouts (LOS).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Autonomous Mission Safety: Empowers astronauts and flight surgeons with real-time anomaly detection and step-by-step emergency protocols when communication with Houston MCC is delayed or unavailable.
  • Proactive Health Management: Mitigates the physiological hazards of long-duration spaceflight—such as fluid redistribution, muscle atrophy, and cardiovascular strain.
  • Deep Space Preparedness: Designed with scalability for lunar Gateway and Martian transit regimes where medical evacuation is impossible.

Development Tools & Technologies

  • Frontend & UI: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
  • Data Visualization & Graphics: HTML5 Canvas for real-time 125 Hz ECG/PPG signal rendering, interactive 3D volumetric CSS/JS wrappers, and Lucide React icons.
  • Architecture: Modular component-based TypeScript architecture with offline local buffering and simulated hardware telemetry streams.

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Immersive Multi-Layered Visualization: Unlike standard dashboards, our 3D volumetric model lets users toggle between hydration, oxygenation, and InBody mass layers to visually inspect internal fluid shifts.
  • Resilience First: Designed with an autonomous "Loss of Signal" (LOS) handling mode, ensuring zero data loss during high-radiation solar storms or orbital eclipses.
  • Human-Centric Factors: The team prioritized high-stress readability, intuitive emergency override triggers, and strict compliance with medical/scientific boundaries (non-diagnostic educational and operational support).
